question: While fully respecting the presumption of innocence, the issuing of six arrest warrants – including one against the President of the Hellenic Basketball Federation – as part of a judicial investigation into alleged bribery and match-fixing raises serious concerns regarding the integrity of sporting competitions, transparency in refereeing and sports federations’ accountability1.

Article 165 TFEU enshrines the promotion of fairness and openness in sporting competitions. The priority areas of the EU Work Plan for Sport 2024-2027 (C/2024/3527) include good governance, integrity and the fight against manipulation of sports competitions. The Macolin Convention, ratified by Greece, establishes a framework to prevent, detect and respond to such practices.
In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

How does it assess the effectiveness of European mechanisms to prevent and detect manipulation of competitions, in particular with regard to transparency in refereeing, federations’ accountability and the independent investigation of complaints?
What specific initiatives does it intend to take to strengthen cross-border cooperation, information exchange and the protection of those reporting corruption in sport?
What results has the initiative planned for 2025 to resolve the deadlock over the EU’s accession to the Macolin Convention yielded, and what further measures are planned?
